propositions: CLI write-command parsers currently use hand-rolled loops with bespoke semantics (--assignee absent=None vs present=""=clear; --force bare/inline/None three-state) that must be migrated to stdlib argparse without changing observable behavior.

argparse defaults (parse_args exit-2 on unrecognized, abbrev matching, built-in help) conflict with existing CLI semantics and must be overridden via add_help=False, allow_abbrev=False, parse_known_args, and custom error() raising CommandError(returncode=1).

transition._parse_flags has three external direct callers (test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py, test_close_ref_target_80af.py, test_dependency_audit.py) that call it directly and unpack its 5-tuple return; it must be retained as a shim to preserve their call sites unchanged.
The retired --force-close flag must be rejected with exit-1 and its historical message (not silently skipped by argparse).

The --force command-specific semantics differ: claim bare --force consumes next non-option token or defaults to "(no reason given)"; transition bare --force sets force_reason="" (None only absent), never consumes a following token, and _force_note() maps it to "(no reason given)" for observable output.
Module-size (<800 LOC), complexity ratchet, make lint, and make typecheck constraints must be met; stale complexity-baseline.json entries must be drained when a function drops below threshold.
